what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat chronic (long-lasting) Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults and children who are at least 3 years old. It works by stopping the Hepatitis C virus from making copies of itself in your body, which helps clear the infection from your liver.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth WITH food every day. Food is very important because it helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, talk to your pharmacist or doctor about other options. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 3 tablets taken together once daily with food. Your doctor will decide the right dose and how long you need to take this medicine based on your specific type of Hepatitis C and your liver health. Treatment typically lasts 8 to 16 weeks, but some patients may need treatment for up to 24 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 18 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember with food. If it has been more than 18 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medicine in its original packaging and away from children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking certain medications that can interact with this medicine, including rifampin (a common antibiotic), carbamazepine, St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), and some cholesterol-lowering drugs like atorvastatin and lovastatin — always tell your doctor and pharmacist about every medicine, vitamin, and herbal supplement you take. Avoid drinking alcohol heavily, as alcohol can damage your liver further. Do not stop taking this medicine early without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well, as this could allow the virus to come back and become harder to treat.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical help immediately if you experience: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark brown or tea-colored urine, light-colored stools, severe tiredness or weakness, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain — these could be signs of liver problems. Also call your doctor if you have signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had Hepatitis B infection, as this medicine may cause Hepatitis B to become active again, which can be life-threatening.
when_it_works: Most people cannot feel the medicine working because Hepatitis C often has no symptoms. Your doctor will check your blood regularly during and after treatment to see how well the medicine is working. Many patients achieve what is called a 'sustained virologic response' (SVR), which means the Hepatitis C virus cannot be detected in your blood 12 weeks after finishing treatment — this is considered a cure. It is important to keep all your lab appointments even after you finish the medicine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy has not been fully studied, so discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: This medicine can be used in children 3 years of age and older, but the dose and form may be different — follow your child's doctor's instructions carefully. Liver Disease: If you have severe liver disease (also called decompensated cirrhosis), this medicine is generally NOT recommended — tell your doctor about your full liver health history. Kidney Disease: Dose adjustments are usually not needed for kidney disease, but always inform your doctor of your kidney health. Older Adults: Older patients can generally take this medicine at the same dose without special adjustments, but should be monitored closely by their doctor.
